name: Nothain
sources: Gwynn, Edward. The Metrical Dindshenchas. Royal Irish Academy, Todd Lecture Series. Dublin: Hodges, Figgis, and Co., Ltd., 1906–1924, 29–31.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Nothain is an Irish heroine. She lost her reason through war, much like Mis and Suibhne in Irish legend. The place poems say she was a fighting lady. An attack killed her whole family and left her mind broken. She walked the countryside unkempt. Her father, the one to survive, searched for her a long time and at last found her, though grief had stolen her speech. She spoke again after a quiet night and asked who was still alive. When she learned no one was, she lay down and died.

Her father, the only survivor, searched more than a year before finding her.
